title: A finitely generated separable field extension is the fraction field of a smooth algebra
statement: Let $K/k$ be a finitely generated field extension [def-pc-field-extension] (i.e. $K=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$) which is separable in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-separable-field-extension]. Then there is a $k$-subalgebra $B\subseteq K$ such that $k\to B$ is a smooth ring map [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and $K$ is the fraction field of $B$, i.e. every element of $K$ is $b/b'$ with $b,b'\in B$, $b'\neq0$ (so $B$ is a domain and $B\to K$ is a localization of $B$ at $B\setminus\{0\}$).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 037X (lemma-localization-smooth-separable, line 44512), implication 'separable => localization of a smooth k-algebra', in the form used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0381 ('there exists a smooth k'-algebra B such that K' is the fraction field of B'); its proof: choose a finite type domain R with fraction field K and apply Lemma Tag 07ND (lemma-smooth-at-generic-point): k -> R is smooth at (0), so R_g is smooth for some g != 0 (Definition Tag 00TB definition-smooth-at-prime)
